Part 2 — Data Visualization

Plot 1 — Age Distribution

p <- ggplot(dfN, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5,
                 fill = "steelblue",
                 color = "white",
                 na.rm = TRUE) +
  labs(title = "Age Distribution of Hospital Patients",
       x = "Age",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 2 — Patients by Sex

p <- dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(sex)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = sex_label)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Hospital Patients by Sex",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 3 — Hospital Admissions by Type

p <- dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(admtype)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = admtype_label)) +
  geom_bar(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Hospital Admissions by Type",
       x = "Admission Type",
       y = "Number of Patients") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 4 — Average Length of Stay by Age Group

p <- dfN %>%
  mutate(age_group = cut(age,
                         breaks = c(0, 18, 40, 65, Inf),
                         labels = c("0-18", "19-40",
                                    "41-65", "66+"),
                         include.lowest = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(age_group) %>%
  summarise(avg_stay = mean(los, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = age_group, y = avg_stay)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(title = "Average Hospital Stay by Age Group",
       x = "Age Group",
       y = "Average Days in Hospital") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 5 — Average Patient Charges by Hospital

p <- dfN %>%
  group_by(provider_label) %>%
  summarise(avg_charge = mean(tot, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(provider_label, avg_charge),
             y = avg_charge)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Average Patient Charges by Hospital",
       x = "Hospital",
       y = "Average Charge ($)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 6 — Hospital Charges vs. Length of Stay

p <- dfN %>%
  filter(!is.na(los), !is.na(tot),
         los >= 0, tot > 0) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = los, y = tot)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, color = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_log10(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Hospital Charges vs. Length of Stay",
       x = "Length of Stay (Days)",
       y = "Total Charges ($, log scale)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Plot 7 — Hospital Charges by Service Category

p <- dfN %>%
  mutate(across(c(trandb, orr, lab, phar, dtest, ther),
                as.numeric)) %>%
  summarise(
    Room_Board = sum(trandb, na.rm = TRUE),
    Operating_Room = sum(orr, na.rm = TRUE),
    Laboratory = sum(lab, na.rm = TRUE),
    Pharmacy = sum(phar, na.rm = TRUE),
    Diagnostic_Tests = sum(dtest, na.rm = TRUE),
    Therapy = sum(ther, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to = "category",
               values_to = "charges") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(category, charges),
             y = charges)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(title = "Hospital Charges by Service Category",
       x = "Service Category",
       y = "Total Charges ($)") +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Animation — Monthly Hospital Admissions by Hospital

library(gganimate)

p <- df2 <- dfN %>%
  group_by(moa, moa_label, provider_label) %>%
  summarise(patients = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(moa) %>%
  slice_max(patients, n = 10, with_ties = FALSE)

ggplot(df2, aes(x = reorder(provider_label, patients),
                y = patients,
                fill = provider_label)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Hospital Admissions: {closest_state}",
       x = "Hospital",
       y = "Number of Patients",
       fill = "Hospital") +
  transition_states(moa_label) +
  theme_minimal()

print(p)

Question 6 — Second Target

Predict whether a patient has a short or long hospital stay.

# Select variables and remove missing values
df4 <- dfN %>%
  select(los, age, sex, raceethn, provider,
         moa, mod, admtype, campus) %>%
  filter(raceethn != "", admtype != "") %>%
  mutate(
    age = as.numeric(age),
    los = as.numeric(los)
  ) %>%
  drop_na()

# Create target
med2 <- median(df4$los)

df4 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(target = factor(ifelse(los > med2, "long", "short"))) %>%
  select(-los)

# Convert categorical variables
df4 <- df4 %>%
  mutate(across(c(sex, raceethn, provider, moa,
                  mod, admtype, campus), as.factor))

# Training 10%, Testing 90%
set.seed(123)

index2 <- createDataPartition(df4$target, p = 0.10, list = FALSE)

train2 <- df4[index2, ]
test2 <- df4[-index2, ]

nrow(train2)
## [1] 12753
nrow(test2)
## [1] 114774
table(train2$target)
## 
##  long short 
##  5441  7312

Question 6 — Decision Tree

tree2 <- rpart(target ~ ., data = train2,
               method = "class",
               control = rpart.control(minsplit = 2, cp = 0.001))

rpart.plot(tree2)

# Variable importance
if (!is.null(tree2$variable.importance)) {
  barplot(sort(tree2$variable.importance),
          horiz = TRUE,
          las = 1,
          col = "steelblue",
          main = "Variable Importance")
} else {
  print("Tree has no splits.")
}

Question 6 — Train and Tune Models

# Decision tree
set.seed(123)

model3 <- train(
  target ~ .,
  data = train2,
  method = "rpart",
  trControl = control,
  tuneGrid = data.frame(cp = c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05, 0.1)),
  control = rpart.control(minsplit = 2, xval = 0)
)

# Random forest
set.seed(123)

model4 <- train(
  target ~ .,
  data = train2,
  method = "rf",
  trControl = control,
  tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = c(1, 2, 3)),
  ntree = 100
)

Question 7

The first classification task predicted whether patient charges were above or below the median. The second task predicted whether a patient’s hospital stay was longer than the median. Decision trees and random forests were trained using 5-fold cross-validation. The models were compared based on accuracy, and the best-performing model was evaluated on the test data.
